value.body: Veterinary pharmaceutical, vaccine, feed-additive and diagnostics companies hire vets for technical and field roles. Typical work includes advising farmers and clinics on products, supporting sales teams with technical knowledge, running field trials, handling product safety reports, and working in diagnostic or QC laboratories.

items.label: Usual entry degree
items.note: 5.5 years including internship; MVSc helps for technical and R&D roles

items.label: Common roles
items.value: Technical / field vet, product executive, lab and QC, regulatory

items.label: Main segments
items.note: Each segment has its own product lines

items.label: Registered veterinary practitioners
items.note: All registered vets in India, not only those in industry roles
items.source: Indian Veterinary Practitioners Register 2023 (VCI), via Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying reply in Parliament

items.label: Livestock population
items.note: Plus ~852 million poultry; the customer base for animal health products

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Usually through campus placements at veterinary colleges, company openings and referrals. A BVSc & AH with registration is the base; field roles value communication and travel, while lab and R&D roles often prefer an MVSc in pathology, microbiology, pharmacology or a related subject.

value.title: At a glance
items: Field and technical-sales roles involve extensive travel to farms and clinics.
Many roles carry sales targets even when the job title is technical.
Experience here can lead to product management, regulatory affairs or diagnostics lab roles.

value.title: Registered veterinary practitioners
value.note: Counts as on 31 March of each year; 2022 not shown. Covers all registered vets, not only those in pharma or diagnostics.
value.source: Indian Veterinary Practitioners Register (VCI), via DAHD replies in Parliament
